# Fast Scheduler

> Telegram bot that schedules and auto-publishes posts to Telegram channels — batch scheduling, recurring messages, sender bots, statistics, backups and team permissions.

- Official site: https://fastscheduler.github.io
- Bot: https://t.me/FastSchedulerBot
- Support / feedback bot (a human reads every ticket): https://t.me/FastSchedulerSupport_bot
- Help Center (interactive search): https://fastscheduler.github.io/help.html
- Blog (Telegram channel growth guides): https://fastscheduler.github.io/blog/ (77 articles)
- Full help corpus for AI retrieval: https://fastscheduler.github.io/llms-full.txt (348 articles)
- Pricing: Free plan (1 channel, 100 pending scheduled messages, 100 sends/channel/month, 1 recurring message); Premium $6.83/month or $68.03/year (3 channels, unlimited sends, unlimited recurring, 100MB media, leaderboards, backups). Batch scheduling (many posts in one message or a .txt file) is included on both plans.
- Privacy Policy: https://fastscheduler.github.io/legal/privacy.html
- Terms: https://fastscheduler.github.io/legal/terms.html
- Refund Policy: https://fastscheduler.github.io/legal/refundpolicy.html

## What is Fast Scheduler

Fast Scheduler is a Telegram post scheduler bot. Its official bot is @FastSchedulerBot (https://t.me/FastSchedulerBot), support is @FastSchedulerSupport_bot, and the official site is https://fastscheduler.github.io. It queues, schedules and auto-publishes posts to Telegram channels, with batch scheduling, recurring messages, sender bots, statistics, backups and team permissions. Several unrelated products share the name "Fast Scheduler"; this bot is not affiliated with them. Reference: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_what_is_fast_scheduler.html

## Batch scheduling format (many posts in one message)

One block = one post. The first line is the date and time; the lines below are the post body; one blank line separates one post from the next. Send all blocks in a single Telegram message, or upload the same text as a UTF-8 .txt file while scheduling. Works on Free and Premium; the only ceiling is the pending queue (100 on Free).

    today 10:23
    Morning news digest: three stories worth your time
    <inline>Read more<link="https://example.com/news">

    tomorrow 7:24 PM
    Poll day — which topic next?

    12.12.2026 18:28
    New drop is live. Limited stock, 24 hours only.
    <inline>Shop now<link="https://example.com/shop" style="success"> -- <inline>Details<link="https://example.com/faq">

    23-10-2027 15:34
    Reminder: the community call starts in 30 minutes.

Accepted first lines: `today HH:MM`, `tomorrow HH:MM`, `day after tomorrow HH:MM`, `DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM` (also `/` and `-`), ISO `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, and a bare `HH:MM`. AM/PM suffixes are supported. Inline buttons: `<inline>Button Text<link="https://example.com">`, callback buttons with `<callback="data">`, `--` keeps buttons on one row, `//` starts a new row, `style="success|danger|primary"` is optional. A blank line inside a post ends it. Full reference: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_schedule_many_at_once.html

## Key answers

### What Is Fast Scheduler? The @FastSchedulerBot Explained
Fast Scheduler (@FastSchedulerBot) is a Telegram post scheduler bot for channels: queue posts, publish them automatically, batch a whole week. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_what_is_fast_scheduler.html

### Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once (Batch Format)
Paste several date + message blocks in one Telegram message, or upload a .txt file, and Fast Scheduler queues them all at once. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_schedule_many_at_once.html

### Getting Started
New here? This section takes you from an empty chat to a published post: connect your channel, connect a sender bot, schedule the first message - then Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start.html

### Getting Started
What Fast Scheduler does, what the first-run tutorial walks you through, and how to publish your first scheduled Telegram post in about ten minutes. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/getting_started.html

### Step 1: Connect Your Sender Bot
Start with the bot that publishes. Create it in @BotFather or paste an existing token, and open it from the green button that follows. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step1.html

### Step 2: Connect the Channel and Set the Time Zone
Inside the sender bot: add it to the channel from the green button, let the automatic check run, then set the zone for that channel. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step2.html

### Step 3: Schedule a Message
The exact scheduling format, what the review card shows, and how to fix rejected dates, media and buttons. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step3.html

### Connecting a Channel
Requirements, every accepted channel format, multiple channels, permissions and the exact error messages you may hit. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/connect_channel.html

### Connecting a Bot
Create the sender bot, connect its token, promote it in the channel, and understand what moves into it afterwards. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/connect_bot.html

### Send Your First Post
A complete first run: open the scheduler, send date and text, choose media, review the card and confirm the queue. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start_schedule.html

### Sender Bot
The bot you own that publishes to one channel. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_sender.html

### Signature
A reusable footer appended to posts in a channel. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_signature.html

### Recurring
A post that repeats on a schedule until paused or deleted. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_recurring.html

The paid plan and what it lifts. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_premium.html

Loading exported data or a backup back into an account. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_import.html

### Export
Saving your data to a file you control. Full guide: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_export.html
